title: Canonical truncation comparisons for t-exact triangulated functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an exact functor, with its shift comparison, and suppose that for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ it sends $\mathcal C^{\le n}$ into $\mathcal D^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal C^{\ge n}$ into $\mathcal D^{\ge n}$. Write $\iota^m:\tau^{\le m}\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}$ and $\pi^m:\operatorname{id}\Rightarrow\tau^{\ge m}$ for the canonical maps. There are unique natural isomorphisms
$$
 \alpha^-_{F,m}:F\tau_{\mathcal C}^{\le m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\mathcal D}^{\le m}F,
 \qquad
 \alpha^+_{F,m}:F\tau_{\mathcal C}^{\ge m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\mathcal D}^{\ge m}F
$$
characterized at each $K$ by
$$
 \iota^m_{FK}\circ\alpha^-_{F,m,K}=F(\iota^m_K),\qquad
 \alpha^+_{F,m,K}\circ F(\pi^m_K)=\pi^m_{FK}.
$$
For any other such functor $G$ and any natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$, the comparisons satisfy, for either sign and its corresponding truncation $\tau$,
$$
 \alpha_{G,m,K}\circ\eta_{\tau K}=\tau(\eta_K)\circ\alpha_{F,m,K}.
$$
The comparison for the identity functor is the identity. If $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ is another exact functor preserving the two halves of bounded t-structures, the comparison for $HF$ is the composite $H(\alpha_F)$ followed by $\alpha_H$ at $FK$.

source.place: Proof, scalar-extension sentence and final automorphism sentence: the implication from preservation of both halves to natural truncation comparison, including natural-transformation and composition compatibility; generic lemma extracted by the agent, not stated as a separate theorem in the blueprint

proof.text:
Fix $m$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], applied to either category, gives the truncation triangles and the adjunctions. Explicitly, for $U\in\mathcal D^{\le m}$ and $V\in\mathcal D^{\ge m}$, the functions
$$\operatorname{Hom}(U,\tau^{\le m}M)\xrightarrow{\iota^m_M\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(U,M),\qquad
\operatorname{Hom}(\tau^{\ge m}M,V)\xrightarrow{-\circ\pi^m_M}\operatorname{Hom}(M,V)$$
are bijections. These are the counit and unit formulations of the stated adjunctions; in particular equality after the displayed composition implies equality before it. All truncation symbols below carry the category of their argument, and $\alpha^{\pm}_{F,K}$ abbreviates $\alpha^{\pm}_{F,m,K}$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), pp. 29–30: adjunctions and their canonical maps

proof.text:
Apply $F$ to the canonical distinguished triangle at the cut $(m,m+1)$ in $\mathcal C$. Exactness in [def-weil-triangulated-category], using the given shift comparison in the last arrow, gives a distinguished triangle
$$F\tau^{\le m}K\xrightarrow{F\iota^m_K}FK\longrightarrow F\tau^{\ge m+1}K\longrightarrow(F\tau^{\le m}K)[1].$$
The endpoint bounds follow from [def-weil-t-structure] and the two preservation hypotheses on $F$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] therefore identifies this triangle with the canonical truncation triangle of $FK$, by an isomorphism equal to the identity on $FK$. Its first component gives an isomorphism $\alpha^-_{F,K}$ with $\iota^m_{FK}\alpha^-_{F,K}=F\iota^m_K$. The first bijection in step 1, with $U=F\tau^{\le m}K$, shows that this equation determines its component uniquely, even among all morphisms.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(ii), pp. 29–30, applied to the image of the triangle at cut m

proof.text:
For the other sign use the cut $(m-1,m)$: the image triangle has endpoints $F\tau^{\le m-1}K\in\mathcal D^{\le m-1}$ and $F\tau^{\ge m}K\in\mathcal D^{\ge m}$. The same exactness definition and clause (1) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] give an isomorphism of this triangle with the canonical triangle of $FK$, identical on $FK$. Its third component is an isomorphism $\alpha^+_{F,K}$ satisfying $\alpha^+_{F,K}F\pi^m_K=\pi^m_{FK}$. Moreover for every $V\in\mathcal D^{\ge m}$, precomposition with $F\pi^m_K$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F\tau^{\ge m}K,V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(FK,V):$$
indeed any map on the left is uniquely $b\alpha^+_{F,K}$ for a map $b:\tau^{\ge m}FK\to V$, and its composite is $b\pi^m_{FK}$, to which step 1 applies. Taking $V=\tau^{\ge m}FK$ proves uniqueness of the lower comparison. These arguments apply to every functor in the statement, including $G$, $H$, and $HF$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), pp. 29–30, at cut m−1; the unit universal property

proof.text:
Let $u:K\to L$. For the upper comparison, naturality of $\iota^m$ and its characterization give
$$\iota^m_{FL}\alpha^-_{F,L}F(\tau^{\le m}u)=F(u)F(\iota^m_K)
=\iota^m_{FL}\tau^{\le m}(F(u))\alpha^-_{F,K}.$$
The common source $F\tau^{\le m}K$ lies in $\mathcal D^{\le m}$. The injectivity from clause (1)'s right adjunction, written in step 1, cancels postcomposition with $\iota^m_{FL}$ and gives naturality of $\alpha^-_F$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary counit calculation using the right adjunction

proof.text:
For the lower comparison compute
$$\alpha^+_{F,L}F(\tau^{\ge m}u)F(\pi^m_K)=\pi^m_{FL}F(u)
=\tau^{\ge m}(F(u))\alpha^+_{F,K}F(\pi^m_K).$$
Here the first equality uses naturality of $\pi^m$ in $\mathcal C$ and the second uses it in $\mathcal D$. The common target $\tau^{\ge m}FL$ lies in $\mathcal D^{\ge m}$, so the left-adjunction injectivity established in step 3 cancels precomposition with $F(\pi^m_K)$. This proves naturality of $\alpha^+_F$. In both signs the componentwise inverses are natural: multiply the naturality equation on the left and right by the relevant inverse components. Thus these natural transformations are natural isomorphisms, and componentwise uniqueness gives uniqueness as natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary unit calculation using the left adjunction
Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary uniqueness calculation for a natural transformation, upper sign

proof.text:
For the lower sign the two morphisms become equal after precomposition with $F(\pi^m_K)$, because
$$\alpha^+_{G,K}\eta_{\tau^{\ge m}K}F(\pi^m_K)
=\alpha^+_{G,K}G(\pi^m_K)\eta_K
=\pi^m_{GK}\eta_K
=\tau^{\ge m}(\eta_K)\alpha^+_{F,K}F(\pi^m_K).$$
Naturality of $\eta$ and then of $\pi^m$ justifies the equalities. The target $\tau^{\ge m}GK$ is in $\mathcal D^{\ge m}$, so step 3's bijection cancels this precomposition. This proves the lower-sign compatibility for arbitrary $\eta$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary uniqueness calculation for a natural transformation, lower sign

proof.text: For $F=\operatorname{id}$ the identity of $\tau^{\le m}K$ satisfies $\iota^m_K\operatorname{id}=\iota^m_K$, and the identity of $\tau^{\ge m}K$ satisfies $\operatorname{id}\pi^m_K=\pi^m_K$. The uniqueness proved in steps 2 and 3 therefore identifies both comparisons with the identity, naturally in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): elementary identity calculation and uniqueness

proof.text:
Let $\beta^{\pm}_K=\alpha^{\pm}_{H,FK}\circ H(\alpha^{\pm}_{F,K})$. These are natural isomorphisms, since each factor is one. For the upper sign,
$$\iota^m_{HFK}\beta^-_K
=H(\iota^m_{FK})H(\alpha^-_{F,K})=HF(\iota^m_K).$$
For the lower sign,
$$\beta^+_K HF(\pi^m_K)
=\alpha^+_{H,FK}H(\alpha^+_{F,K}F(\pi^m_K))
=\alpha^+_{H,FK}H(\pi^m_{FK})=\pi^m_{HFK}.$$
Here the inner truncations and canonical maps are in $\mathcal D$ and the outer ones in $\mathcal B$. The composite $HF$ is exact with its composite shift comparison and preserves both halves: apply the corresponding properties first for $F$, then for $H$. Uniqueness in steps 2 and 3 for $HF$ gives $\beta^{\pm}=\alpha^{\pm}_{HF,m}$, as required.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii): elementary composition calculation and uniqueness

proof_origin.place: Elementary t-exact-functor consequence of Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), pp. 29–30; exact/t-exact terminology in 1.3.16, p. 36. The natural-transformation and composition equations are written out by the worker.
